claim: The RLM paper describes RLMs as a general inference paradigm in which long prompts are treated as part of an external environment.
quote: We propose Recursive Language Models (RLMs), a general inference paradigm that treats long prompts as part of an external environment and allows the LLM to programmatically examine, decompose, and recursively call itself over snippets of the prompt.

claim: A follow-up study (SRLM) treats the long context as an external variable accessible within a sandboxed execution programming environment.
quote: treat context as an external variable accessible within a sandboxed execution programming environment.

claim: Context-centric approaches instead shrink what the model reads: the In-context Autoencoder compresses a long context into short compact memory slots that can be directly conditioned on by the LLM.
quote: compress a long context into short compact memory slots that can be directly conditioned on by the LLM for various purposes.

claim: Highlight-Then-Summarize takes a compress-then-reason route, first identifying question-relevant evidence and then integrating it into a compact summary.
quote: We propose Highlight-Then-Summarize (H2S), a compress-then-reason paradigm that first identifies source-grounded, question-relevant evidence and then integrates it into a compact, question-conditioned summary before producing the final answer.

claim: The Chained RLM authors state that the RLM approach improves long-context inference without changing model weights.
quote: This improves long-context inference without changing model weights

claim: The survey notes that gist-token methods typically require modifying the parameters of the LLM.
quote: However, such methods typically require modifying the parameters of the LLM.

claim: On output quality, the original RLM paper reports strong results against common scaffolds at comparable cost.
quote: dramatically outperform the quality of vanilla frontier LLMs and common long-context and coding scaffolds (e.g., on GPT-5 by a median across the evaluated benchmarks of $26\%$ against compaction, $130\%$ against CodeAct with sub-calls, and $13\%$ against Claude Code) across four diverse long-context tasks while having comparable cost.

claim: Later work qualifies this. SRLM authors report that recursion is not the main driver of RLM performance.
quote: Our findings show that recursion itself is not the primary driver of performance in RLM, and a simple self-reflective program search can match or surpass RLM without requiring self-query or explicit recursion mechanisms.

claim: A reproduction study found that deeper recursion degraded performance and inflated time and token costs.
quote: applying deeper recursion (depth=2) or using RLMs on simple retrieval tasks paradoxically degrades performance and exponentially inflates execution time (e.g., from 3.6s to 344.5s) and token costs.

claim: The λ-RLM authors also criticise open-ended REPL code generation as hard to verify and predict.
quote: Yet existing RLMs depend on an open-ended read-eval-print loop (REPL) in which the model generates arbitrary control code, making execution difficult to verify, predict, and analyse.

claim: On cost for the context-centric side, Cartridges match in-context learning with far less memory.
quote: On challenging long-context benchmarks, Cartridges trained with self-study match ICL performance while using 38.6x less memory and enabling 26.4x higher throughput.

claim: Evidence from coding agents warns that fewer tokens do not guarantee lower cost.
quote: The largest compression setup reduced delivered tool-output tokens by 38.4% but increased billed cost by 6.8%, while lighter compression produced only small and statistically uncertain savings.

claim: The same study found that aggressive compression reduced successful patch application on a SWE-bench Go subset.
quote: On a SWE-bench Go subset, aggressive compression also reduced successful patch application.

claim: In Chained RLM, intermediate artifacts from each staged computation can be inspected, corrected, and extended by a later fresh inference by the same model.
quote: in each staged computation, intermediate artifacts can be inspected, corrected, and extended by a later fresh inference by the same model.

claim: One paper notes that no published empirical study has tested how codebase scale drives context growth and tool-call degradation in agentic coding systems.
quote: Despite these convergent findings, no published empirical study has directly tested the joint hypothesis that codebase scale drives context window growth, which in turn triggers measurable MCP tool attrition
